claims.text: Polycrystalline copper has a face-centered cubic structure.
Polycrystalline copper exhibits temperature-dependent plastic deformation.
The temperature dependence of plastic deformation in polycrystalline copper is caused by thermally activated dislocation motion and grain-boundary interactions.
The proposed initial material has an average grain size of 10 micrometers.
The proposed initial material has a dislocation density of 10^12 m^-2.
The proposed initial material has an average grain-boundary misorientation of 30 degrees.
The material will be subjected to uniaxial tensile deformation at a constant strain rate of 0.001 s^-1.
Testing will span 300 K to 800 K with a heating or cooling rate of 5 K/min and a temperature-exposure duration of 30 minutes.
Dislocation density and grain-boundary misorientation mediate the temperature-dependent deformation response.
Increasing temperature increases dislocation mobility through thermally activated dislocation glide.
Increased dislocation mobility and enhanced grain-boundary sliding decrease yield stress and flow stress at higher temperatures.
The yield stress is predicted to be 200 MPa at 300 K.
The yield stress is predicted to be 140 MPa at 800 K.
The flow stress is predicted to be 200 MPa at 300 K.
The flow stress is predicted to be 140 MPa at 800 K.
The yield stress at 300 K is predicted to be 30% higher than at 800 K.
Lower temperatures reduce dislocation mobility and grain-boundary sliding, thereby increasing yield stress and flow stress.
The exact yield-stress and flow-stress values depend on material processing and testing conditions.

contradictions.description: The stated stresses of 200 MPa at 300 K and 140 MPa at 800 K make the 300 K value approximately 42.9% higher than the 800 K value, not 30% higher. A change from 200 MPa to 140 MPa is instead a 30% decrease relative to the 300 K value.

The predicted flow stress at 800 K is 140 MPa, but the hypothesis is declared falsified if that flow stress is greater than 130 MPa. Thus, the stated prediction itself satisfies the falsification condition.
